plausibility_notes: Justin admits carrying a small bottle in his map sleeve and removing it beside Grant's glass. The lab found an unmarked waste bottle with compatible cyanide residue. That combined opportunity and object association makes him the strongest suspect.

There is no ownership mark, fingerprint, chemical exclusivity, bottle identification, exact contact time, or link placing Justin at the cabinet theft. His bottle could still have an innocent function not specified in this release.
Al held the empty target glass and Brie wiped its exterior. Neither action is excluded by the clear shared punch or by their economic explanations; contamination of an empty glass remains viable.
Hugh and Tess have admission receipts after the theft report, weakening personal theft theories but not proving they could not use already-stolen poison or an accomplice.

The final release conspicuously explains every other suspect's suspicious object or statement, then leaves Justin with the single unexplained small bottle. The lead has a factual basis but is made much stronger by the writing pattern than by exclusive evidence.
